0.name: Cultivation
0.notes: Soil + water + sunlight -> ripe olives on tree. 2.5M ha, 340M trees, 75% Andalusia. Climate stress and land fragmentation (380K farms avg 7ha) are the main D-constraints. Strong cooperative model (Dcoop, Hojiblanca) provides C.

cap_income_share_pct.source: CDE/University of Bern — Lea Lamotte fieldwork

0.scope_source: Not provided — agricultural emissions data requires separate data input

1.name: Harvesting
1.notes: Ripe olives on tree -> harvested fruit. Vibradoras (mechanical shakers) + nets. Nov-Jan window (3 months). Dcoop: 75K families. Good years: 8,000 kg/day; drought years: 1,000 kg/day (2022). 15% seasonal worker shortage in 2023.

seasonal_worker_shortage_pct.source: Spanish Ministry of Agriculture / Bottega del Sarto 2025

1.scope_source: Not provided — harvesting machinery emissions require separate data input

2.name: Milling and Processing
2.notes: Olives -> crude olive oil + alperujo. Cold mechanical extraction: wash, crush, malaxate, centrifuge. No heat or solvents for EVOO. 1,755 mills. Largest at Villacarrillo (Jaen): 2,500t/day. Acesur AI Easy Taste: 600 samples/day. C slightly exceeds D: technology is contribution-dominant at this phase.

ai_quality_samples_per_day.source: Deutsche Bank / Acesur 2025 — Easy Taste AI device

2.scope_source: Not provided — milling energy emissions require separate data input (Acesur uses solar-powered mills)

3.name: Waste and Byproduct Recovery
3.notes: Alperujo -> pomace oil + compost/fertilizer + biomass fuel. Spain is world leader in pomace oil. Professional Organization of Olive Pomace Oil recognized 2016. C-dominant: the circular economy integration delivers more contribution than constraint at this phase. ~0.8t alperujo per tonne of olives milled.

alperujo_uses.value: fertilizer; biomass energy; animal feed; pomace oil extraction
alperujo_uses.source: Business Insider / Dcoop 2023; Olive Oil Times Pomace 2016

3.scope_source: Not provided — byproduct recovery emissions require separate data input

4.name: Storage
4.notes: Crude olive oil -> stable stored bulk oil. Nitrogen-blanketed stainless steel tanks, constant temperature, total darkness. Dcoop: world's largest facility at 300,000 MT (1/3 of an oil tanker). Up to 2 years shelf life. C-dominant: world-class infrastructure delivers more than constraint at this phase.
4.scope_source: Not provided — cold storage energy emissions require separate data input

5.name: Packaging and Bottling
5.notes: BOTTLENECK. Bulk oil -> bottled product. ~67% of Spanish exports leave as bulk (EUR 3.22/kg avg) then rebranded by Italian firms at EUR 4.42/kg (+EUR 1.20/kg). 1,500 fragmented bottlers. Glass cost +25% globally. Spain lacks coordinated brand strategy. Retail prices (Tesco own-brand EUR 3.95/L) compress margins. D significantly exceeds C: institutional and competitive constraints dominate.

filippo_berio_uk_market_share_pct.source: Sustainable Food Trust 2018 — Salov rebranding Spanish bulk oil

5.scope_source: Not provided — bottling line energy emissions require separate data input

6.name: Bulk Logistics and Export
6.notes: Bottled or bulk oil -> delivered to international buyers. MSC flexibag (24,000L per 20ft container). Rubino RS intermodal tank containers (road+rail, ISO 9001/14001/GMP+). Short-sea Spain-Italy corridor (24-48h). Red Sea disruptions +10-15 days to Asia (late 2024). Container rates 2-3x pre-pandemic.

red_sea_delay_days.source: Bottega del Sarto — Supply Chain Challenges 2025

container_rate_vs_prepandemic.source: Bottega del Sarto — Supply Chain Challenges 2025

6.scope_source: Not provided — shipping emissions (bunker fuel) require separate data input

7.name: Trade and International Markets
7.notes: Delivered oil -> sold at retail or foodservice. Italian brands capture EUR 4.42/kg from Spanish bulk at EUR 3.22/kg. Fraud history (Italian-sounding brands on Spanish oil). Retail oligopoly (Carrefour/Tesco/REWE hold >50% shelf). Record EUR 6.04B exports in 2023/24 but driven by price spike not brand premium. Growing USA and Asia demand. D exceeds C: brand and market structure constraints dominate.
7.scope_source: Not provided — retail/distribution emissions require separate data input

system.interpretation: Spanish olive oil supply chain is robust from cultivation through storage (phases 0-4, balance 88-95%) but structurally fails at Packaging/Bottling (Phase 5, balance 81.1%) and Trade/Markets (Phase 7, balance 85.5%). The core problem: Spain produces ~51% of global olive oil but captures only EUR 3.22/kg average export price vs Italy's EUR 4.42/kg because two-thirds of exports leave as undifferentiated bulk. Italian companies (Salov/Filippo Berio, Deoleo/Bertolli) blend and rebrand at premium, capturing EUR 1.20/kg that Spanish producers forfeit. On record EUR 742,500 tonnes exported in 2023/24, this represents approximately EUR 890M in foregone annual revenues.
